notes: LANDED kb/Work PB1123. Every verb that stores several operands of ONE statement with no verb-specific timing rule identifies them once, in source order, before the first read or store, through the ONE mechanism PlaceIdentification.Freeze (hoisted by PlaceIdentification.Hoister): UNSTRING (INTO, DELIMITER IN, COUNT IN, POINTER, TALLYING; its MOVE stores rebuilt over the frozen places by BoundMove.Retargeted), STRING (senders, receiver, POINTER), INSPECT, INVOKE (receiver, arguments, RETURNING, universal path) and CALL, whose private hoist copy is deleted in favour of the same mechanism. UNSTRING S INTO I UE(I) stores UE(1), WITH POINTER PE(I) delivers into PE(1). EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED 2026-11-10: in force at 85 in part, the reference-modification step standing after subscript evaluation and after function evaluation, §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR3 'a. If subscripting is specified for the operand, the reference modification is evaluated immediately after evaluation of the subscripts.' and 'c. ... immediately after evaluation of the function.'; the closing sentence the notes above argue (item identification as the first operation of the statement, identifiers left to right) is stated by no general 1985 rule this adjudication found (1985 times subscript evaluation statement by statement), the 2002 token rests on §2002:14.5.4, which prints that sentence, and the 2014 token is forced by the validator and rests on no 2014 text read.
